name: Emmahono
body: We will have a few days in Funchal with our seven-year-old, and I am trying to plan one afternoon that still works if rain interrupts our outdoor plans. We will be staying near the centre, so we can walk a little, but I would rather avoid a long transfer for a single activity. A museum followed by a short cafe stop might work, provided neither needs advance booking that locks us into a fixed hour. If the weather clears, we could add a garden or a waterfront walk. I am less sure which places are genuinely engaging for a child and which are better suited to adults reading every display. A relaxed meal matters more to us than another stop, because an overfilled itinerary usually falls apart by mid-afternoon. One starting point for local ideas was [url=https://madeiraguide.top]madeira island blog[/url] but I would value advice from people who know what is open and practical this season. Which part of town would you focus on for a flexible afternoon? We can change the order on the day and are happy to skip a stop if the weather or our child's energy changes. An easy place to take a break would make a difference, and we would appreciate any recent notes about opening hours or awkward steps with a stroller. A small plan we can actually enjoy is enough.
